properties.digitized_from: Pier 70 Design for Development, Figure 6.4.2 - Maximum Building Height (p.155).
properties.digitization_method: REDONE 2026-09-14: the previous version of this polygon was traced using a transform fit from 5 street intersections plus Historic Building 12's real footprint as a 6th anchor. A user-flagged visual comparison against satellite imagery showed the resulting blocks were systematically rotated/sheared (~13-14 degrees off, and not even mutually orthogonal) relative to the real street grid -- confirmed by comparing traced block bearings against the real, independently-surveyed Building 14 footprint (DataSF Building Footprints, blklot 4052001), which sits at the real street grid's true orientation (~356/86 degrees, consistent with SF's known ~4-degree grid skew). Root cause: an error in the original corner-correspondence matching, not a diagram-scan distortion. REBUILT using a fresh 6-point affine transform: 5 real street-intersection control points (20th St x Illinois St, 20th St x Michigan St, 21st St x Illinois St, 21st St x Michigan St, 22nd St x Illinois St -- fetched from OpenStreetMap via this project's own src/fetch_streets.py) plus the real, independently-confirmed centroid of Historic Building 12's own Assessor parcel (blklot 4114010) as a 6th, spatially-distant anchor. This fit has a residual error of 1-8m against its own 6 control points (far tighter than the previous transform), AND was validated by checking that it reproduces the correct real-world bearing (independently confirmed via Building 14's footprint) rather than just checking point-position error, which is what let the previous version's shear go undetected. Pixel corners for this block were re-read directly from Figure 6.4.2 with fresh, fine-grained crops. Residual error against the 6 control points is roughly 1-8m; treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m given the additional (small) error from reading this specific block's own corners off the diagram. RE-TRACED 2026-09-16 (full Pier 70 geometry restart, after a systematic pass found 9 of this site's other 'trusted' parcels were meaningfully wrong): a fresh programmatic color-trace (RGB [128,193,219]) matched this block's old area closely (~75800 vs ~75400 px2) but only ~44% by IoU -- the old shape was a similar size but shifted/rotated relative to the true diagram fill. Re-measured programmatically instead of by eye: isolated this legend color and extracted its precise 7-vertex contour (OpenCV), capturing the block's real angled SW corner near the PG&E switchyard. Converted via the same validated 6-point affine transform. Confirmed zero overlap with HDY1/2 or H1. CLIPPED 2026-09-17 (found via join_approximate.py's new MAJOR CLIP warning, prompted by user-flagged issues elsewhere): confirmed via direct satellite comparison that this block's west/SW portion sits on a real, currently-paved curving driveway near the PG&E switchyard (visible pavement with a clear curb), not vacant land -- 34% of this block's area was inside the buffered real-street layer. Clipped via shapely difference() against the corrected real-street buffer, same pattern already used for Parcels D/E1/H1/H2/E4; area dropped from ~7,260 to ~4,815 sq m. EXTENDED 2026-09-17 (user-flagged: 'F/G can expand a beat east to Louisiana like its northern neighbors'): this block's own north-facing boundary (the notch left by the driveway clip above) dipped 6-45m west of the Louisiana St offset line that C1/C2 now front (9.8m west of the real centerline) -- a real, if modest by area, discrepancy against the '...like its northern neighbors' standard. Pushed the notch's own vertices (the ones between the SW switchyard corner, left untouched since that's a distinct, separately-confirmed real driveway curve, and the point already east of the line near C1/C2) out to the Louisiana offset line at each vertex's own latitude; several of the resulting points landed within a meter of each other (since the pushed edge is now close to straight) and were simplified away (shapely simplify, ~0.05m tolerance) rather than left as a stack of near-duplicate vertices. Confirmed 0 overlap with C1 and C2. Area drops from ~4,815 to ~3,548 sq m, despite this being an eastward 'expansion' -- the removed notch was a westward bulge (the driveway-clip trace curving further west than the Louisiana line, not a dent cutting into the block), so pulling that curve back east to a straight, Louisiana-aligned edge nets less area even though the edge itself moved toward the target frontage. Visually, this reads as the north edge now sitting flush with C1/C2's own Louisiana frontage instead of bulging west of it.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land, surface parking, or an existing industrial building slated for demolition within Brookfield's 28-acre district (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Redone 2026-09-14 with a corrected, shear-free transform (see digitization_method) -- treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 5-15m, not survey-grade. NOTE: this polygon is NOT clipped against real streets or existing buildings -- unlike Potrero's approximate blocks, several of Pier 70's D4D blocks are sited on existing industrial buildings that will be demolished, so overlap with a currently-real building is often expected, not an error; a boundary that appears to touch or slightly cross a street centerline reflects this transform's 1-8m residual error, not a deliberate encroachment.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of Brookfield's larger, largely unaddressed 28-acre site), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named parcels -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead.
properties.regulatory_context: Commercial office/life science, shown as ONE combined parcel 'F/G' in the D4D's own Figure 6.4.2 (not two separate parcels 'F' and 'G'), 90 ft max, 6 stories per D4D Section 6.4.2. Brookfield's own leasing brochure gives an exact combined total of '+/- 410,000 RSF' for F-G, Phase 2. No construction-start source found.
properties.notes: Approximate polygon for a real, D4D-adopted parcel -- see accuracy_caveat.
